title: SOME/IP: Simplifying the TP Header Parser Code
description: This might speed up the code and make it easier to understand it.

notes.body: mentioned in merge request !12236

My comment before was that I think you should be able to use proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint(...., &tp_offset) to save the separate assignment at line 3716 below.  There are times when you want to know the value before you add the item, but I think it could work here.

No, this does not work here due an API limitation in Wireshark or at least I do not see how.

proto_tree_add_xyz calls mask and shift, if `bitmask != 0`, which makes sense but this field it does not work, since the value is not shifted but the lower 4 bits need to be filled with zeros. So currently I do not see a way - maybe missing something - to do this without `tvb_get_ntohl`.


What was quite surprising to me: `proto_tree_add_uint` will also mask and shift all values you pass to it, if bitmask!=0. I assume the reason for having `proto_tree_add_uint` and others was to allow non-standard behavior, so that the dissector can code the behavior that is needed. Unfortunately, I do not see how this should work, when `bitmask != 0`.

I was checking, if other dissectors use `proto_tree_add_uint` and expect masking and shifting. I found for example https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/dissectors/packet-6lowpan.c
At a first glance that code needs cleanup as proto_tree_add_item should have been used anyhow. So one can assume that the masking and shifting is not really necessary.

The following ways could improve the API:
- change the behavior of `proto_tree_add_uint` and others. A lot of work and risk.
- add a parameter for this to `proto_tree_add_uint` and others. Also quite some work but less risk.
- create new alternatives to `proto_tree_add_uint` and others. Makes the API bigger.

What do you think?

> I was checking, if other dissectors use proto_tree_add_uint and expect masking and shifting.

An example: SCCP had an issue where it used `proto_tree_add_uint` and did its own masking and shifting, but also set `bitmask != 0`, and did not expect the number to be shifted again, which caused a reported issue. That was fixed in fb845cc4c483bbbbc2ebdc65998220cdd02aa7ee by switching to `proto_tree_add_item`.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12254/diffs?diff_id=798259523&start_sha=a7844bf04b0762448392c2487ab0eefc31f5c2dd#939d770822ae6ea95241591ea801aa75281c2840_3717_3716)

So someone else got confused by `proto_tree_add_uint` and bitmask. :smile: 

Only that in this case `proto_tree_add_uint` was not really needed. Probably the case with most dissectors out there that use that call.

Unfortunately, this does not work for me. But I created a new workaround. See below.

Hi Lars,

I believe you are misunderstanding the intent of this API.

`proto_tree_add_uint` is for when you already have the value you want to appear in the field, like with a generated field or where the value is not exactly what is stored in the frame (e.g. subject to a multiplier).  The tp offset fieldis masked because it is a subset of a 32-bit word, but it can be added directly with 'proto_tree_add_item'.

I was suggesting that you instead use

'proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint'

This would shift and mask the value our of the tvb (as 'proto_tree-add_item' does), but as a convenience also retrieve the value into the uint32_t address of the last arg given.  Then you could avoid the extra fetch (using tvb_get_ntohl) and mask.

Hi Martin,

I surely stumbled over this API. :smile: 

> `proto_tree_add_uint` is for when you already have the value you want to appear in the field

The issue is that `proto_tree_add_uint` does not do what you wrote above, when bitmask is active. It does not use the value passed in but the value is masked and shifted it first. :disappointed: 


> The tp offset field is masked because it is a subset of a 32-bit word, but it can be added directly with 'proto_tree_add_item'.
I cannot use `proto_tree_add_item` as this does not work either for my case. I need to multiply the value with 16 first (left shift 4).


Maybe an example helps to understand my problem or you can see were I am wrong:

Value of 32bit field in packet: 0x0000 0021 (this includes also reserved and more segments flag)

Lets split it:
- More segments flag: True (1)
- Reserved: 0
- Value of 24bit field in packet: 0x0000 002

Specifications says: 0x0000 002 of the offset part means 0x0000 0020 (lower 4 bits are assumed 0, basically multiply with 16)

If I use `proto_tree_add_item` with bitmask, it ends up with 0x0000 0002. Since it shifts 4 bits to the right and I cannot multiply the value. So this does not work for me. `proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint` has the same problem, hasn't it?

If I use `tvb_get_ntohl` to get the value, mask out the lower 4 bits, and do not shift, I get 0x0000 0020, which is correct.
When I put this value (0x0000 0020) into `proto_tree_add_uint` I have to different options:
- bitmask is defined as 0: would work but does not show the 24bits in Wireshark and just a plain number. So I cannot show this as a bitmask line.
- bitmask is defined as 0xffff fff0. But this does not take the value I pass directly but masks the value first and shifts it 4 bits right. So I end up with 0x0000 0002, which is wrong.

As you said above the `proto_tree_add_uint` should allow to calculate the value first, so that you can transform it first. This is currently not the case for `bitmask != 0`. IMHO, the current behavior does not make sense as you cannot freely transform the value of a field that is a bitmask.

The API covers the most common use cases (hopefully :-) ) where you probably want the actual subfield value.
In cases like this you may have to fetch the value and opertate on it. That said you could have used
..ret_uint and shifted the value by 4.

This is right but I wanted the filter to have the calculated value.

I guess one could create an addition calculated field for the real value and make the filter names in a way that people understand. That could potentially remove the need for using `tvb_get_ntohl` but it is not much simpler.

Possible alternatives:

`proto_tree_add_bits_return_value()`

or add all three of the fields with

`proto_tree_add_bitmask_list_ret_uint64` and then apply your mask to the return values to get the values.

Better?

A generated field for the result after multiplying seems reasonable.

I think in your particular case you could get it to work with `proto_tree_add_uint_bits_format_value()`

Doing almost the same thing as you're doing now. You would have a zero bitmask and pass in a formatted string for the value.

I tried that `proto_tree_add_uint_bits_format_value` (see line after Encoded Offset):

```
    SOME/IP-TP: 000005716c6d6e6f707172737475767778797a7b7c7d7e7f808182838485868788898a8b…

```

And this would really be good for adding the calculated offset.

Only one issue: there are double spaces between bytes (also in UI not only when copying text), while for `proto_tree_add_item`. What am I doing wrong here?
resolved all threads

I propose to keep the simplification as proposed by the patch.

The API is currently what it is.

While changing the API might make sense - at least to me and the authors of packet-sctp, I understand that this would require to check all dissectors affected first.
